So the question really is how do we take what we've heard
and what we've learned and turn it into action
as the project moves forward?
So to do this, we developed a set of guiding principles to steer us through future phases of the project.
Those are discussed in detail in attachment B.
And there are four guiding principles.
Each one is accompanied by an intention and three objectives.
And, of course, all of these guiding principles are in the context of the work we're doing to evolve our energy business,
to continue to be financially successful, and provide valued services.
So the first guiding principle focuses on Kitchener Utilities as a business.
and for that we will make responsible, accountable and financially rewarding business decisions.
Our intention there is really to work to responsibly position our community-owned utility
for success as things change around us.
And the three objectives under that guiding principle
are around following sound business practices,
taking action quickly to manage risk and maximize opportunity
and to assess value holistically to find our best contribution.
The second guiding principle really focuses on our customers.
And so we'll serve customers as an affordable and reliable partner in the energy transition.
Our intention there is to work to empower customers and community members as their trusted partner in this work.
And those objectives focus on pursuing affordable, reliable and predictable energy services,
empowering customers with choice and with trustworthy, accessible information,
as well as bringing people along as things change more broadly.
The third guiding principle focuses on those broader community goals that the city has
and that come through our community owned utility as well.
For that we will contribute to a thriving community and our intention is to work to
make the community even stronger.
Specific objectives there are to collaborate with partners, do our partners to address
climate change and use clear metrics and align them with community scale goals.
Now, of course, there are things we know and there are things we don't know about what our energy system will look like in the future.
So the fourth guiding principle is really about preparing for the different ways our energy system could change.
And so we will plan for multiple energy futures with flexibility and focus.
And our intention there is to prioritize solutions that can adapt to and provide value in all different energy futures.
Specific objectives there are to rely on safe bet technologies and prepare for long shot technologies.
as well as preparing for a broad range of net zero carbon futures,
and more broadly, iterating, experimenting, and learning as part of our approach.
So, taking together these guiding principles and the more specific objectives with them
are how we want to take what we've learned and act on it.
And this is really the guiding light for the work that comes next
as we gear up for looking at specific options in phase two.
